deals.evidence: A trio of local owners have taken control of LAFC
deals.headline: Local trio Berg, Beck and Rosenthal take control of LAFC as managing owners
deals.investor: Larry Berg, Brandon Beck and Bennett Rosenthal
deals.summary: Larry Berg (then Apollo senior partner) became lead managing owner with Brandon Beck (Riot Games) and Bennett Rosenthal (Ares) as co-managing owners; all three had been limited partners. Founding managing partner Henry Nguyen became vice-chairman and owner. No price or stake was disclosed.

deals.evidence: participated in a $180-million syndicated loan with other banks funding stadium construction
deals.headline: $180m syndicated bank loan funds construction of LAFC's $350m stadium
deals.investor: Bank syndicate including Banc of California
deals.summary: Banc of California, which also took a 15-year stadium naming deal (later unwound in 2020), participated with other banks in a $180m syndicated loan funding construction of the privately financed $350m stadium. Bloomberg, via MLSsoccer.com, reported the loan was collateralised solely by stadium revenue, the first such MLS stadium loan.

deals.evidence: in a deal that values the club at more than $700 million
deals.headline: LAFC owners buy half of Vincent Tan's 20% stake at a record $700m-plus valuation
deals.investor: A handful of existing LAFC owners
deals.summary: A handful of current owners bought half of Malaysian businessman Vincent Tan's 20% stake and planned to buy the other half internally, in a deal valuing the club at more than $700m, then an MLS record. The size of the half-stake (10%) is arithmetic, not stated, so stake_pct is left blank.

deals.evidence: More than a half-dozen investors have sold out of their equity
deals.headline: LAFC buys out more than half a dozen minority investors to trim its cap table
deals.seller: Tony Robbins, Paul Schaeffer, Allen Shapiro, Jason Sugarman, Kirk Lacob, Mark Leschly and others
deals.summary: After entering 2022 with about 30 investors, the largest cap table in MLS, LAFC bought out more than six small shareholders and began raising new money at a valuation just under $900m. Exit prices were not disclosed.

deals.evidence: Adam Freede has purchased a minority stake in LAFC
deals.headline: Adam Freede buys a minority stake in LAFC
deals.summary: Freede bought from the pool of equity created by the 2022 buyouts; neither he nor LAFC disclosed the stake or valuation (the club had been raising at just under $900m). LionTree advised Freede.

deals.evidence: saw the incoming shareholders purchase 6% of LAFC’s equity at a $1.25 billion valuation
deals.headline: Joe Tsai and Mike Mahan exit as Carlos Vela, James Cha and Juan Domingo Beckmann buy 6% of LAFC at $1.25bn
deals.investor: Carlos Vela, James Cha (Spring Oak Partners) and Juan Domingo Beckmann Legorreta (Becle)
deals.summary: Three new limited partners bought 6% of LAFC's equity at a $1.25bn valuation while Brooklyn Nets owner Joe Tsai (an investor since 2016) and Fanatics Collectibles CEO Mike Mahan (since 2014) left. Sportico named Cha and Beckmann in August 2026.

founded_evidence: Founded in 2014, LAFC made its MLS debut four years later after paying a then-record expansion fee of $110 million.
name: Los Angeles Football Club
notes: Replaces the earlier record's Wikipedia capacity source; the Forbes valuation is kept ($1.32bn) and now cited through the Internet Archive snapshot of the Forbes list because forbes.com article pages refuse automated fetches (the live forbes.com/teams/lafc/ page shows the same $1.32B, $167M revenue and $14M operating income). Forbes' revenue and operating income (EBITDA) estimates reflect the 2025 season. Sportico values LAFC at $1.4bn (+9%, February 2026) and puts 2025 revenue at $158m. Owner rows: the club publishes no percentages, so every stake_pct is blank; valuation_at_entry for Vela, Cha and Beckmann is the $1.25bn (USD) price of the 6% deal they bought into. Larry Berg is no longer on the club's ownership page but still holds his shares until he sells them (Sportico reported in August 2026 that MLS has given him two years to sell; Rosenthal expects existing owners, and possibly outside capital, to buy). No private-equity fund, sovereign or other institutional vehicle holds LAFC equity; several owners are principals of investment firms (Ares, Oaktree, Gaw Capital, Benchmark, Spring Oak) investing personally. LAFC's own outbound investments, not deals in LAFC: majority owner of Grasshopper Club Zurich since January 2024, an investment in FC Wacker Innsbruck, the Red&Gold Football joint venture with Bayern Munich (2023), and a small stake in NWSL's Angel City FC acquired via warrants in 2024. Expansion fee: $110m, paid before the club's 2018 debut (pre-2015 award, not listed as a deal). The club says it has sold out every MLS regular-season and playoff match (January 2023 release), but no average attendance figure was found. Not found on a citable page: registered legal entity, social-media follower counts, and stake percentages for any owner.

ownership_summary: LAFC is owned by a group of individual investors with no published percentages: 28 shareholders listed by the club plus Larry Berg. Bennett Rosenthal (Ares Management co-founder) has been lead managing owner since 2023 and is due to hand the role to co-managing owner Brandon Beck (Riot Games co-founder) in 2027. Berg, a founding partner and managing owner, was named MLS commissioner in August 2026 and has two years to sell all his shares. Peter Guber is executive chairman. Limited partners include Will Ferrell, Magic Johnson, Mia Hamm and Nomar Garciaparra, and Ares' Mike Arougheti and Oaktree's Bruce Karsh invest personally. No fund or corporate vehicle holds a stake, and MLS waived its rule that a club's control person hold at least 35%.
